documented: MySQL documents mysql:// for the classic protocol and mysqlx:// for X Protocol, with user[:password]@ userinfo. Passwords may be omitted or explicitly empty and neither is an exposed nonempty password.
Reserved component characters must be percent-encoded. Hosts can be names, IPv4 or bracketed IPv6; Unix socket paths can be percent-encoded or parenthesized. IPv6 zone separators use %25.
X DevAPI documents mysqlx+srv:// with a single DNS SRV hostname and no explicit port or Unix socket.

MySQL query attributes include parenthesized path strings and bracketed lists. Connector/J separately defines JDBC scheme variants and per-host property grammars; those distinct forms are outside this rule.
assumptions: The detector recognizes exposed nonempty literal passwords, not valid accounts, reachable services, successful authentication, or complete client configuration. No verifier or DNS call is made.

Each full candidate is capped locally at 16 KiB. Whitespace and double-quote/backtick/angle-bracket carriers delimit candidates; matching apostrophe wrappers are removed contextually while apostrophes inside URI components remain legal. Malformed suffixes and invalid percent escapes are rejected rather than truncating to a valid prefix.

Framing precedes percent-escape validation. No whole-value or recursive decoding is used. A valid percent escape represents a nonempty credential byte, including encoded NUL; these rules do not copy libpq's C-string restrictions.

Host parsing checks bracket, separator and URI-component framing, not DNS spelling, IPv6 address validity or reachability. Ports retain decimal syntax but have no numeric range restriction: a port unusable by a client does not make a literal password public. Unknown query options and unrelated option values do not suppress an exposed password.
JDBC and nested scheme prefixes are excluded. Scheme-less connection strings, attribute names and arbitrary query text are not credential evidence.
Only the explicitly prefixed lowercase mysql, mysqlx and mysqlx+srv forms and nonempty userinfo passwords are recognized; no password is inferred from query-only password text.
Socket coverage includes percent-encoded paths and parenthesized Unix paths. Windows named-pipe syntax and Connector/J host-property credential structures are not inferred.
The presence of a literal password is retained even with an empty username or default/empty host; no authentication-method or user-account constraints are imposed.
evidence.fixture_method: Hand-constructed deterministic synthetic URI values with reserved .invalid names, documentation IP ranges, local socket paths and invented one-character or escaped passwords. No real deployment credentials are used. Boundary, malformed-full-candidate, public/passwordless, exact-cap, over-cap and later-candidate cases defend native recognition rather than successful connections.

documented: MongoDB defines mongodb:// and mongodb+srv:// connection strings with a single username:password userinfo before the host information.
The connection-string specification requires escaping at-signs, extra colons and malformed percent signs in userinfo; RFC 3986 component characters supply the supported raw alphabet.

Standard host information supports comma-separated hosts with independent ports, bracketed IP literals and URL-encoded Unix sockets. SRV replaces that list with one hostname and forbids an explicit port.
A slash separates host information from optional database and query options. Authentication passwords are supplied in userinfo rather than a generic password query option.

documented: The Redis provisional URI registration defines redis:// and describes rediss:// as the TLS variant with the same credential semantics. Userinfo uses user:password and an exact password query key can supply the AUTH password.

redis-cli documents redis://user:password@host:port/dbnum, percent-encoded passwords and default as the default username. Its pinned URI parser additionally defines [[username:]password@], including password-only userinfo and empty/default hosts.
URI hosts and paths are optional. The registered path has zero or one segment representing a nonnegative decimal database number.

Values embedded in unrelated options, case variants and semicolon-separated lookalikes do not establish password evidence. Any nonempty password assignment is retained even when another value overrides it.

documented: RabbitMQ defines amqp:// and amqps:// for AMQP 0-9-1. Userinfo is username[:password] and username/password allow unreserved, percent-encoded and sub-delimiter characters.
Absent credentials differ from explicit empty values. Empty usernames and hosts are allowed by the ABNF, and any nonempty password in userinfo is the supplied SASL password.

The virtual host is one URI path segment; slash characters within its name must be percent-encoded. Query parameters may configure TLS/connection settings but the URI specification does not define a general password query option.
